name: Vertical chin lengthening

card.summary: Genioplasty (or a graft or implant) that makes the chin taller rather than just more forward; documented in the surgical literature, mostly as small case series.
card.aka: Lengthening genioplasty, vertical genioplasty, chin lengthening
card.note: Techniques using grafts carry infection, donor-site and bone-resorption risks described in the literature.

quick.overview:
Vertical chin lengthening is a set of surgical methods that increase the height of the chin, usually by cutting the chin bone and inserting a graft or spacer, or by using an implant. Surgeons describe it for short lower faces, including in East Asian contouring surgery.

The published evidence is largely technique descriptions and case series rather than controlled trials.
quick.mechanism: In an osseous genioplasty the chin segment is cut, moved down, and held in place, with a bone graft or other material filling the gap. Variants combine lengthening with narrowing. Alloplastic implants can also add height.
quick.risks: The literature mentions infection, donor-site problems and resorption of grafted bone as drawbacks of graft-based methods. It is a surgical procedure performed by licensed surgeons.

lead: Vertical chin lengthening refers to surgical techniques that increase the vertical height of the chin, as distinct from advancing it forward. Methods described in the literature include osseous genioplasty with interpositional bone grafts, pedicled grafts, and alloplastic materials. [1][2][3]

Authors describe the operation for patients with a short lower face or a short and wide lower face, particularly in East Asian aesthetic surgery, where it may be combined with narrowing of the chin. [1][2] A report from 1987 discusses lengthening and shortening of the chin by adding or removing bone and states that results improved with miniplate fixation. [3]
No randomized trials of vertical chin lengthening were found; the evidence consists of technique papers and retrospective series. [4][5]
infobox: Interpositional bone graft, pedicled graft, implant

paras: A 1987 review of altering the vertical dimension of the chin discusses subtraction and addition of bone, and describes a preferred technique using an interpositional bone graft from the outer table of the calvarium. [3]

A 2014 paper from East Asia describes a novel narrowing and lengthening genioplasty for lower-face contouring, intended to avoid disadvantages of autogenous bone grafts or alloplastic materials. [1] A 2013 paper describes a pedicled interpositional graft for short, wide lower faces, aimed at reducing infection, donor-site morbidity and graft resorption. [2]

A 2020 paper presents a new osteotomy technique for vertical lengthening genioplasty. [6] A study of interpositional allogenic (iliac) grafts examined whether lengthening with such grafts is safe and effective. [7]

The authors of the pedicled-graft paper list infection, donor-site morbidity and height loss through graft resorption as problems of conventional graft methods. [2] A review of 262 consecutive genioplasties performed with bimaxillary surgery reported outcomes and complications of osseous genioplasty in general. [4]

A 2026 retrospective cohort examined the effect of aesthetic osseous genioplasty on upper airway volumes. [8] An encyclopedic summary of chin surgery notes that donor bone appears linked to higher infection rates. [9]

Published studies are technique descriptions and retrospective case series, including 262 consecutive osseous genioplasties with bimaxillary surgery [4], pedicled and novel narrowing-and-lengthening techniques [1][2], an iliac-graft evaluation [7] and a 2020 osteotomy technique. [6] No controlled trials of vertical lengthening were identified.

timeline.event: A review of shortening and lengthening the chin reports improved results with miniplate fixation and calvarial grafts. [3]
Pedicled interpositional graft for narrowing and lengthening genioplasty described. [2]
A novel narrowing and lengthening genioplasty is published. [1]
New osteotomy technique for vertical lengthening genioplasty described. [6]
